title: A finite extension of an algebraically closed field is trivial
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $K$ be a field together with a ring homomorphism $\varphi:k\to K$ making $K$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. Then $\varphi$ is bijective, i.e. an isomorphism of fields.

source.place: Fields, Lemma (lemma-algebraically-closed), tag 09GR, (1)⇒(2): every irreducible polynomial over an algebraically closed field is linear; for $a\in K$ the minimal polynomial of $a$ over $k$ (which exists since $K$ is finite over $k$) is irreducible, hence linear, so $a\in\varphi(k)$
